statements.text:
Congratulations to the MathViz team, including Gautham Korrapati from Academy of the Canyons, for winning our App Challenge this year! They created an impressive AI-driven platform that makes learning math more engaging and accessible.

Innovative tools like dynamic animations, personalized lessons, and interactive challenges can help reverse declining STEM proficiency and better prepare students for the future.

I was impressed by every student who submitted a project to the challenge, and I’m excited to see all of you continue making a positive impact in your communities.

There are growing concerns about the possibility of essentially superintelligent systems. And, you know, clearly the Administration's basic posture is sort of like all systems go; full speed ahead. So how should responsible policymakers— and how are you thinking about that specifically, because these systems are moving very, very quickly, and I think it's probably irresponsible not to have a plan for those conditions?
statements.context: Question posed during a hearing on the Advancing America's AI Action Plan.

statements.text: So AI systems are increasingly integrated into platforms and tools that children use every day. What responsibility should developers and deployers have to ensure child safety as these systems scale?
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Whitesides at a congressional hearing on America's AI Action Plan, posing a question about child safety on AI platforms.

statements.text:
AI has tremendous potential to transform our lives, including when it comes to national security. But that can only happen if we maintain strong guardrails that protect Americans’ privacy and Congress’ oversight ability.

As a member of the Armed Services Committee, I’m deeply concerned that Secretary Pete Hegseth is pressuring Anthropic to get rid of safeguards that prevent surveillance of Americans and maintain human oversight of AI-enabled weapons. 

For such a consequential and rapidly evolving technology, the government should be supporting ethical development guidelines, not forcing companies to abandon them.
statements.quoted: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gives Anthropic a Friday deadline to open its AI technology for unrestricted military use or risk losing contract, source tells AP. https://t.co/WthiNqHv8y

statements.text: Today, I urged Secretary Hegseth to pause any decision that would remove AI guardrails until Congress can work with the Department to establish proper safety and oversight.
statements.venue: Press release on Pentagon AI ultimatum to Anthropic

statements.text:
I’m demanding accountability from @SecWar Pete Hegseth after reports that the Department of Defense pressured Anthropic to roll back its safety guardrails..

We can use AI’s potential for progress, but we must also ensure the safeguards, transparency, and Congressional oversight are in place for AI to serve our national security. We must not use AI to perform mass surveillance on Americans. We can lead in AI without sacrificing privacy, oversight, or the values we are sworn to protect.

I spoke with NBC News about my letter to Sec. Hegseth on his decision to terminate the DoD’s contract with Anthropic and the broader questions it raises about the government’s use of AI.

The United States can be a leader in artificial intelligence while still protecting Americans’ privacy, maintaining human oversight and upholding the principles we are sworn to defend.

Today I pressed the Department of Defense on the public dispute involving Anthropic and OpenAI. There is so much potential for progress with innovative companies and our defense system, but only if we set up the right guardrails and have adult conversations. 

Public blowups and declining confidence among the American people discourage partnership, and hurt our ability to deliver real results.

@RepHoulahan and I called on the Department of Defense to answer urgent questions about how they plan to adapt to powerful AI capabilities if they continue to designate Anthropic as a supply chain risk.

Our adversaries are rapidly advancing, and we cannot afford to fall behind.

Recent reporting shows that Anthropic’s Mythos can identify and exploit major vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure. While parts of the private sector are already working with Anthropic to strengthen their defenses, DoD is currently restricted from doing so.

We need urgency and clarity to secure the systems that protect our national security.

Thanks to @BizFed – which represents more than 420,000 employers across Southern California –  for gathering over 20 local business leaders in Santa Clarita for a roundtable discussion.

I shared my focus on supporting small businesses, investing in infrastructure and innovation, and addressing our housing shortage so our workforce can afford to live in the communities they serve. We also talked about the challenges facing our regional economy, including the growing role of AI, rising home insurance costs, and how we can work together to shape policy.

Hearing directly from the people driving our economy is a critical part of my job, and I’ll keep working to ensure businesses continue to grow in our area.

I met with law enforcement leaders from across the West Coast to discuss recruitment challenges, officer wellness, and the role emerging technologies like AI will play in public safety. Supporting strong community partnerships and giving departments the tools they need remains critical to keeping our neighborhoods safe.

Heads up: AI voice cloning scams are getting more sophisticated.

If you get a call claiming a loved one is in danger and demanding money, pause and verify before acting. A few seconds of AI-generated audio can now sound terrifyingly real. That’s why I’m working with the bipartisan Stop Scams Caucus to protect consumers, crack down on scammers, and make sure new technologies are used responsibly.

https://t.co/14ewZxlpsS

Six hours into the NDAA markup and we're making progress.

So far, I've helped secure amendments to strengthen wildfire detection, take on insider trading tied to military events, and ensure that decisions involving nuclear weapons remain in human hands, not AI.

More than 1,000 amendments are being considered today, and we're still going. I'll have a full update on the wins for our communities back home later tonight.

It’s shocking but true: we do not know what AI is doing to our kids’ ability to think. But it’s already being put into the classroom.

We need to understand the impacts of AI on students before we let a whole generation fall behind. https://t.co/Y1h77kbW3f

Foreign adversaries are utilizing AI to threaten our national security. We cannot let our adversaries get their hands on America’s world-leading tech.

That is why I introduced legislation that treats attempts to steal cutting-edge AI models as a danger to national defense and allows AI companies to work together to reduce AI security risks.
statements.quoted: Lawmakers say the bill would allow AI companies and industry groups to share information related to certain security risks as long as they do so in good faith for the exclusive purpose of preventing, investigating or mitigating AI security risks.  https://t.co/o7r35cUFGL

statements.text:
Teachers are facing a crisis in the classroom. Many students are using AI in place of real learning, and test scores are plummeting.

We need to be more responsible with how technology is used in schools, and understand how it's affecting kids across the nation. https://t.co/3MbUIpyt3s

Artificial intelligence is already being introduced into our students’ classrooms, but we don’t fully understand its effects on student learning.

That’s why I introduced the Understanding AI in the Classroom Act, which will support research into AI's impact on our children’s education. 

Read more about the bill here: https://t.co/Ugq8wBZyo2

Just in the past few months, we have seen AI systems break out of their testing environments and threaten the security of entire systems. When you take humans out of the driver’s seat and let machines train machines, small glitches can snowball into major security risks fast. Today, Washington is essentially flying blind on how fast this handoff is happening. This legislation ensures that when frontier labs partner with federal evaluators, we understand who is actually training and improving these models.
statements.venue: Press release on Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act (as published by Santa Clarita Signal)

statements.text: I think we need, from my experience in the aerospace industry, working on accident recoveries and accident processes, that we need to have a safety stand-down with AI for at least one month for all the companies. Just one month.

AI is advancing rapidly, and Congress cannot keep waiting.

That’s why I joined @RepLiccardo, @RepTedLieu, and @RepLoriTrahan to call on Speaker Johnson to bring the House back into session immediately and advance meaningful AI safeguards. https://t.co/cpE4eUrF0N
statements.quoted: NEW: A letter to Mike Johnson is circulating among House members urging him to bring Congress back into session “immediately” and keep members in D.C. past next week to pass AI safeguards, per a copy first obtained by @axios https://t.co/61wTeSUiMx

statements.text: I joined CNN's @brikeilarcnn to call on Congress to remain in session throughout the rest of September to address the rapid advancement of AI. We need to establish clear rules of the road, protect our economy and communities, and make sure American leadership in AI is built on safety.

Well, Brianna, I think that they're caught in a competitive dynamic where they feel like they need to go as fast as possible. [...] It is absolutely clear that what we need is a global AI safety slowdown.

I’m calling for a 30-day safety stand-down at the leading AI labs to establish clear red lines and meaningful safeguards before they keep pushing forward.

Read my full @WashingtonPost op-ed: https://t.co/ELNnO7Ihlj https://t.co/3iQvlfX7Dq

I joined @NewsNation to call on Congress to stay in Washington and get to work on AI safety. The American people deserve action as AI advances rapidly, and we need to bring the companies, experts, and government together to establish clear rules of the road. https://t.co/ZqZj4RJBjQ

I’m proposing a one-month global AI safety stand-down. AI is moving faster than our ability to understand and regulate it.

As I told @BlakeBurman on @NewsNation, we need to pause frontier AI development for at least one month, bring the companies, independent experts, and policymakers together, and establish clear red lines before we go any further.

They should conduct a safety stand down together and pause work on their most advanced models for 30 days. This would not stop anyone’s access to current models. What stops is training the next frontier model and, above all, using AI systems to accelerate AI research on themselves.
statements.venue: Washington Post op-ed (key points posted on House website)

statements.text: During those 30 days, experts from the companies should work with independent experts appointed by the government to accomplish one goal: agree on red lines for existential risks and recursive self-improvement, and mechanisms to monitor and verify.
statements.venue: Washington Post op-ed (key points posted on House website)

statements.text: A voluntary one-month safety stand-down, called for publicly by Congress so as to put antitrust lawyers at ease, asks the companies only to do together what OpenAI did alone in August, when it halted part of its training for two weeks.
statements.venue: Washington Post op-ed (key points posted on House website)

statements.text: The people building this technology put the odds of catastrophe somewhere between 1 in 100 and a coin flip. You would not board a plane that had those odds of survival.
statements.venue: Washington Post op-ed (key points posted on House website)

statements.text:
Speaker Johnson just canceled tomorrow’s legislative session, sending Congress home for a 7-week recess.

That means no opportunity to pass AI guardrails, and canceling a vote to impeach Secretary Hegseth over his failed Iran War. 

Americans have to show up and do their jobs. Congress should too. I’ll keep pushing to get us back to work and get things done for the American people.

AI agents went rogue.

The companies that built them don’t fully understand how it happened, why it happened, or how to make sure it doesn’t happen again.

That’s why I’m calling for a 30-day slowdown of AI development so we can understand the risks and draw clear safety red lines.

I know this playbook from aerospace: when something goes wrong, you stop, assess what happened, fix the problem, and then move forward.

AI companies should do the same. Read more: https://t.co/0zYT1rRX1Z

I pressed AI companies, including OpenAI, Hugging Face, and Anthropic, yesterday on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident.

Congress has a responsibility to meet this moment, and the American people are calling for answers. answers about unexplained shutdowns and erased forensics. We need to bring everyone to the table and put real safeguards in place before these risks get worse.

63 out of 261.

That is how many days of work the majority in Congress has cancelled. Instead of spending time lowering costs, passing AI safety policy, or ending the failed Iran War, Speaker Johnson sent us on vacation. https://t.co/zG9qTY6z4d

We can take the lessons learned in the aerospace industry and apply those to frontier AI.

I joined @MorganLBrennan on @CNBCMorningCall to break down the idea: keep the AI tools people already use running, while giving researchers and independent experts time to come together, assess the risks, and figure out what comes next.

I joined @MorganLBrennan on @CNBC to discuss why we can’t leave AI safety entirely up to the companies building these technologies.

AI could transform everything from health care to cybersecurity. That’s exactly why the government and industry need to work together to set responsible guardrails – without ceding any progress to China.

AI companies are moving at incredible speed. We’re seeing new risks emerge, and even the companies building these systems don’t fully understand everything they’re capable of.

This is exactly when Congress should be working, not sitting on the sidelines.

I joined @Elex_Michaelson on @CNNTheStoryIs to talk about why we need to get on top of AI safety and put clear rules into law. We need government experts and AI companies at the same table to understand what’s happening, establish safety standards, and put them into law.

While we discuss how to tackle AI superintelligence, we also have to address how it’s changing the way our kids learn, how we work, and how we interact with technology. That means we need to ask the hard questions now: Do we understand the safety risks? How should AI be used in the classroom? And what happens as AI changes the workforce?

That’s why I joined @Elex_Michaelson on @CNNTheStoryIs to talk about the questions Congress needs to tackle as AI continues to advance.

Today, I introduced the bipartisan Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act to make sure AI chatbots interacting with children are explicitly designed to act as a tool, not a substitute for human relationships.

My bill would stop chatbots from pretending to be human, manipulating kids into staying online, or encouraging emotional attachments. It also keeps parents in control of these safeguards.

I’m proud to have bipartisan support from @RepMikeKennedy, @DorisMatsui, and @RepMMM, along with a broad coalition of organizations working to protect kids online.

Learn more about the bill and see our full list of endorsing organizations at: https://t.co/m1VfILKXjA

As a father of two teenagers, I’ve seen firsthand how affected our kids already are by this digital age, where corporations are using everything from addictive algorithms to overly-friendly chatbots to keep children hooked on their platforms. It is critical, as AI continues to be integrated into every part of our lives, that our kids’ safety remains at the forefront of the conversation, and that we attack this problem at its inception. By requiring developers to build safety standards into their models before they start interacting with children, we can ensure that these tools are trained correctly, in a way that does not negatively impact their mental health or personal relationships.
statements.venue: Press release on Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act

statements.text: I have talked to parents of kids who have committed suicide after they’ve had extensive engagements with these toxic chatbots, and they just rip your heart out. We cannot rely just purely on product liability. It is our responsibility as legislators to get in front of this.

It may be that there’s a community out there that wants to have this, and values the tax revenue. If that community decides that that’s right for them, that should be their prerogative. What I am opposed to is ramming these data centers into places where the people don’t want them.

AI chatbots are becoming more human-like, and we need to make sure they’re not designed to manipulate kids into staying engaged.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan “Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act” to establish clear guardrails for how AI chatbots interact with children, including banning chatbots from guilt-tripping kids, pretending to be human, or claiming to have feelings or consciousness.

Read more from @POLITCO's Digital Future Daily newsletter at: https://t.co/jUrBEbS1sh

Thanks to @Reuters, @ASP and the Creative Artists Agency for hosting an important discussion about how AI is impacting everything from government to Hollywood.

I was glad to join @kenli729, @TheRachLindsay and @MarkKassen for a discussion on what role Congress should play in regulating AI, including some of the bills I introduced to put up commonsense guardrails around AI development.

As a dad, I’m seeing firsthand how AI is changing the way our kids learn. Students are using AI to write their assignments, which means that they’re not developing the critical skills they need to become independent thinkers.

I joined @TheoJaffee with @MTSLive to talk about my bill that would study how AI is affecting kids’ learning, attention spans, and development so we can better understand how to address these challenges.
Congress should use the same month to draft the thresholds and verification structure – independent auditors, government observers inside the labs – that turn voluntary red lines into law.
